rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Youth, free time, and wealth can ruin a person; one should spend age, youth, and riches on the true aim.
rows.anchor: فعكسوا الأمر وكان ينبغي لهم أن يصرفوا العمر والشباب والغنى في تحصلي المطلوب الحقيقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited Persian couplet presents love, youth, and revelry together as the desired set whose combination enables eloquent expression.
rows.anchor: عشق وشباب ورندى مجموعه مرادست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The outward command is to stop disputing after repeated invitations met only refusal and arrogance; the Persian gloss says to turn away from their requital until ordered to fight.
rows.anchor: فأعرض عن جدالهم فقد كررت عليهم الدعوة فأبوا إلا الاباء والاستكبار

rows.speaker: فتح الرحمن
rows.claim: Another explanation takes the command as turning away from excessive concern for them and grief that consumes the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وفي فتح الرحمن فتول عن الحرص المفرط عليهم وذهاب النفس حسرات

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wāsiṭī reads the withdrawal as leaving them to the happiness or misery assigned to them in pre-eternity.
rows.anchor: وقال الواسطي ردهم إلى ما سبق عليهم في الأزل من السعادة والشقاوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is not censurable for withdrawing after exhausting his effort and exceeding every customary limit in conveying the message; malāma means censure.
rows.anchor: بذلت المجهود وجاوزت في الإبلاغ كل حد معهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word al-lawm and malāma mean reproach or censure, glossed in Persian as blame.
rows.anchor: واللوم والملامة العذل وبالفارسية نكوهيدن

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: Some spiritual elders say the Prophet cannot guide those he loves; he conveys the message, while guidance is not his responsibility.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض الكبار فتول عنهم فإنك لا تهدي من احببت منهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another inward reading makes withdrawal a journey toward God: convey the message and means of salvation outwardly while remaining present to the divine Essence without being veiled.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم فتول عنهم بسيرك إلينا فما أنت بملوم في إبلاغ رسالتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means to continue reminders and admonition, not abandon them altogether; the implied object pronoun is omitted because it is evident.
rows.anchor: أي افعل التذكير والموعظة ولا تعدهما بالكلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the command means 'remind them'; the object pronoun is omitted because the context makes it clear.
rows.anchor: أو فذكرهم وقد حذف الضمير لظهور الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers are either those whose faith God has decreed or those who have already believed; reminders increase their insight and certainty, and admonition softens hard hearts.
rows.anchor: أي الذين قدر الله إيمانهم أو الذين آمنوا بالفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should keep receiving instruction despite the unbelievers' obstinacy, since counsel has many benefits and softens hard hearts.
rows.anchor: فإنها تزيدهم بصيرة وقوة في اليقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited hadith says every believer repeatedly falls into a familiar sin, since believers are forgetful and tested, but remember when reminded.
rows.anchor: ما من مؤمن إلا وله ذنب قد اعتاده الفينة بعد الفينة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: For the obedient, a reminder is news of abundant reward; for gnostics, it recalls the afflictions God has spared them.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : ذكر المطيعين جزيل ثوابي وذكر العارفين

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A further Sufi gloss says reminders warn sinners of punishment so they return, encourage the obedient with reward, and renew lovers' witnessing of divine beauty and majesty.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : ذكر العاصين منهم عقوبتي ليرجعوا عن مخالفة أمري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author allows an angel to combine spiritual power with a wing suited to its realm, whether birdlike or otherwise; reason and sensory form can coexist in accord with wisdom and power.
rows.anchor: ولا منع من أن يجمع الملك بين قوة روحانية وبين جناح يليق بعالمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's night ascent represents total annihilation: night manifests fanāʾ, and its seven stages correspond to seven divine names, ending with al-Qayyūm and al-Qahhār.
rows.anchor: أن النبي عليه السلام إنما عرج ليلة الإسراء بالفناء التام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night symbolizes annihilation and day subsistence; the seven annihilation stations correspond to seven names, while Mecca's seven sanctuary minarets signify them.
rows.anchor: ولذا وقع الإسراء في الليل الذي هو مظهر الفناء دون النهار الذي هو مظهر البقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's sanctuary has five minarets for the five subsistence stations signified by the five remaining names, ending in al-Ahad al-Samad.
rows.anchor: ولذا جعلت مناراته خمسا على عدد مراتب البقاء التي أشير إليها بالأسماء الخمسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calculates seven names at one hundred each, giving seven hundred; Gabriel's lower annihilation station stops at the Lote Tree, while the Prophet proceeds to the Throne and overcomes it.
rows.anchor: كل واحد من تلك الأسماء السبعة مائة على حسب تفصيلها إلى الأسماء الحسنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel's journey ends at the name al-Qayyūm, where the Prophet's course subdues him; Gabriel remains to convey revelation that gives hearts life, hence his title Spirit of Holiness.
rows.anchor: فانتهى سير جبريل إلى الاسم القيوم فصار مقهورا تحت سير النبي عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel has six hundred of the seven hundred wings in image and meaning, while the Prophet has seven hundred spiritual wings; prophetic power therefore exceeds angelic power and Gabriel receives strength from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: فله من تلك الأجنحة السبعمائة ستمائة صورة ومعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author supports this hierarchy by citing that God's hand is above their hands, and says Gabriel, as one of the hands, receives strength from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقد قال تعالى : يد الله فوق أيديهم وإن جبريل لكونه من الأيدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The horizon phrase is circumstantial, describing the subject of istawā as being at the highest horizon.
rows.anchor: حال من فاعل استوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The horizon is the boundary between visible and unseen portions of the celestial sphere; the upper horizon is sunrise, unlike the lower western horizon, so Gabriel is at the eastern edge of the world.
rows.anchor: والأفق هي الدائرة التي تفصل بين ما يرى من الفلك وما لا يرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Am is a disconnected question with the sense of bal, shifting from the opponents' baseless fancy to the point that it gives them no benefit; the hamza negates and rebukes.
rows.anchor: أم منقطعة وما فيها من معنى بل للانتقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tamannī is forming an imagined object within oneself, through guesswork or based on observation; because it often rests on conjecture, falsehood commonly governs it.
rows.anchor: والتمني تقدير شيء في النفس وتصويره فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person does not obtain everything he desires, including the idolaters' empty hope that their gods will intercede; a cited poem says winds thwart what ships want.
rows.anchor: ليس للإنسان كل ما يتمناه وتشتهيه نفسه من الأمور التي من جملتها أطماعهم الفارغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poem illustrates disappointed wishes: a person does not attain everything he desires, as winds drive ships contrary to their wishes.
rows.anchor: ما كل ما يتمنى المرء يدركه

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kāshifī takes 'man' to mean the disbeliever, who wishes for idol intercession or complains that prophethood was not given to a particular person.
rows.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : آياهست مر انسان را يعني كافررا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported explanation is that a person wishes for long life and for there to be no resurrection or gathering.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أم للإنسان ما اشتهى من طول الحياة وأن لا بعث ولا حشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inward allusion is humanity's capacity for perfection through annihilation of selfhood and subsistence through God; bodily and spiritual attachments obstruct it, so one does not attain every wish and each is eased toward its created end.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى أن للإنسان استعداد الكمال وهو الفناء عن أنانيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People cannot wish themselves into being manifestations of opposite divine attributes; the text invokes God as First and Last, Manifest and Hidden, whose unity encompasses apparently opposed determinations.
rows.anchor: وإنما تمنى لما ليس له مخلوقية على صورة من جمع الضدين

rows.speaker: الخراز
rows.claim: Asked how he knew God, al-Kharrāz answered that he knew Him through the joining of opposites: manifestations differ while the underlying reality is one.
rows.anchor: وسئل الخراز قدس سره : بم عرفت الله؟ قال : بالجمع بين الضدين

rows.speaker: الحسين
rows.claim: Al-Husayn says choice seeks lordship and wishing seeks escape from servanthood; God's punishment of servants comes when their wishes are granted.
rows.anchor: قال الحسين رحمه الله : الاختيار طلب الربوبية والتمني الخروج من العبودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's exclusive ownership of both afterlife and present world explains why a person is not guaranteed the fulfillment of every wish.
rows.anchor: تعليل لانتقاء أن يكون للإنسان ما يتمناه حتما فإن اختصاص أمور الآخرة والأولى جميعا به

words: وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything in the heavens and earth belongs to God by creation and ownership, exclusively, without independent or shared ownership by another.
rows.anchor: أي خلقا وملكا لا لغيره أصلا لا استقلالا ولا اشتراكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reward clause attaches to the sense of God's knowledge, while the intervening words are parenthetical; universal creation establishes His knowledge of people's states and their just recompense.
rows.anchor: الخ متعلق بما دل عليه أعلم الخ وما بينهما اعتراض مقرر لما قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the straying and guidance of both groups and recompenses wrongdoers with punishment for their misguidance, here called their evil deeds.
rows.anchor: فيعلم ضلال من ضل واهتداء من اهتدى ويحفظهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wrongdoers are repaid with punishment for their misguidance, which the text calls their evil deeds.
rows.anchor: أي بعقاب ما عملوا من الضلال الذي عبر عنه بالإساءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who do good are the guided, and God rewards them with the best recompense, namely Paradise.
rows.anchor: أي بالمثوبة الحسنى التي هي الجنة فالحسنى للزيادة المطلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-husnā may mean an unqualified increase; the bāʾ either makes the verb transitive or marks cause and recompense.
rows.anchor: فالحسنى للزيادة المطلقة والباء لتعدية الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about avoiding major sins may qualify 'those who do good' or replace it; Saʿdī al-Muftī objects that treating it as the focus leaves the earlier phrase idle.
rows.anchor: صفة للذين أحسنوا أو بدل منه لكن قال سعدي المفتي

rows.speaker: سعدي المفتي
rows.claim: Saʿdī al-Muftī considers the parsing awkward if 'those who avoid' is the main focus and 'those who do good' is effectively omitted; reversing the order would work.
rows.anchor: قال سعدي المفتي : لا حسن في جعل الذين الخ مقصودا بالنسبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Avoidance is purification, which comes before adornment; its present tense indicates continuous practice. Believers must habitually avoid sins to merit Paradise, whereas one voluntary good deed earns reward even once.
rows.anchor: يقول الفقير : الاجتناب من باب التخلية بالمعجمة وهي أقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Major sins are offenses with grave punishment and a specific threat, including idolatry, adultery, and murder, especially killing one's own buried-alive daughters.
rows.anchor: الإثم ما يكبر عقابه من الذنوب وهو ما رتب عليه الوعيد بخصوصه

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr defines major sins as those for which the sinner does not seek forgiveness, citing the saying that no major sin remains with repentance and no minor sin with persistence.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جبير : هي ما لا يستغفر منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith warns against treating sins as trivial; Ibn ʿAbbās estimates major sins at nearly seventy, and the commentary refers to an earlier discussion in Sūrat al-Shūrā.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : هي إلى سبعين أقرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fawāḥish are especially shameful major offenses, particularly adultery and unlawful killing; naming them after major sins specifies grave examples within the general category.
rows.anchor: وما فحش من الكبائر خصوصا الزنى والقتل بغير حق

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib defines fāḥish, faḥshāʾ, and fāḥisha as acts or words of great ugliness.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : الفحش والفحشاء والفاحشة ما عظم قبحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lamam denotes approaching a sin without committing it, and by extension a minor sin; the exception is disconnected because minor sins are outside the major sins and are forgiven when major sins are avoided.
rows.anchor: اللمم مقاربة المعصية ويعبر به عن الصغيرة من قولك الممت بكذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Five daily prayers, one Friday to the next, and one Ramadan to the next expiate intervening sins when major sins are avoided; good deeds erase evil deeds.
rows.anchor: يعني أن الصلوات الخمس والجمعة إلى الجمعة ورمضان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view calls an unintentional glance lamam, but a repeated deliberate glance is sinful; it also includes a wink or kiss.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هي النظر بلا تعمد فإن أعاد النظر فليس بلمم

rows.speaker: نبهان التمار
rows.claim: Nabhān the date seller embraced and kissed a customer who came to buy dates; she rebuked him, he regretted it, and went to the Messenger.
rows.anchor: كما روى أن نبهان التمار أتته امرأة لتشتري التمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation limits lamam to a sinful thought that crosses the heart without a firm resolve.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هي الخطرة من الذنب أي ما خطره من الذنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view defines lamam as any sin for which God has specified neither a legal penalty nor punishment.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كل ذنب لم يذكر الله عليه حدا ولا عذابا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say lamam is a sin committed from time to time, without becoming a settled habit or persistent practice.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : اللمم والإلمام ما يعمله الإنسان الحين بعد الحين

rows.speaker: محمد بن الحنفية
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyya says every good or evil intention is lamam, citing the Prophet's report that Satan and the angel each prompt a person; Satan whispers and the angel inspires.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن الحنفية : كل ما هممت به من خير وشر فهو لمم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says lamam is a single lapse into indecency followed by repentance without persistence; the exception is then connected, and God accepts repentance.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما معناه إلا أن يلمم بالفاحشة مرة ثم يتوب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās cites Abū Hurayra's Prophetic report: the eye, lips, hand, and feet each have a share of adultery; the genitals either consummate or deny it, and without consummation it is lamam.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : ما رأيت شيئا أشبه باللمم مما نقله أبو هريرة

rows.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
rows.claim: Al-Asʾila al-Muqḥima says all sins are major in the absolute sense because they disobey God, though some are greater relatively; shirk is greatest, and lamam is major if it means a sin whose perpetrator repents, as Mujāhid, al-Ḥasan, and Companions including Abū Hurayra say.
rows.anchor: وفي الأسئلة المقحمة الذنوب كلها كبائر على الحقيقة لأن الكل تتضمن مخالفة أمر الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's forgiveness is vast enough to cover minor sins when major sins are avoided; this explains the exception and shows they are exempt through forgiveness, not because they are no sins.
rows.anchor: حيث يغفر الصغائر باجتناب الكبائر فالجملة تعليل لاستثناء اللمم

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Najmī gloss identifies three major attachments: the commanding self, desire that fans the self's fire, and worldly life, the root of wrongdoing; their obscenities are violating law for nature, loving worldly pleasures, and turning from God toward other things.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية : كبائر الإثم ثلاث مراتب : محبة النفس

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: In that reading, lamam is a slight humanly necessary inclination toward self, desire, or the world, such as bodily rest and a modest worldly share taken as a right rather than selfish gain; fulfilling rights is forgiven, while pursuing gratification is delusion.
rows.anchor: قوله إلا اللمم أي الميل اليسير إلى النفس والهوى والدنيا بحسب الضرورة البشرية

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Sufi gloss sees vast forgiveness as covering the darkness of metaphorical existence with the light of real existence through annihilation of human nature and subsistence through divine identity.
rows.anchor: ومن سعة غفرانه ستر ظلمة الوجود المجازي بنور الوجود الحقيقي

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: A spiritual elder says legitimate worldly obligations, such as serving people or thanking them for benefits, do not impair servanthood; egoistic worldly aims without divine command do and require returning to God.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الكبار : من استرقه الكون بحكم مشروع كالسعي في مصالح العباد

rows.speaker: بعض العارفين
rows.claim: Some gnostics reason that a believer who sins under threat of punishment must feel regret; since the Prophet says regret is repentance, that remorse cancels the threat, while the believer combines good and bad deeds.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض العارفين : من المحال أن يأتي مؤمن معصية توعد الله عليها بالعقوبة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The cited Prophetic saying declares that remorse is repentance, supporting the view that a believer's regret cancels the threatened punishment.
rows.anchor: وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم الندم توبة

rows.speaker: بعض العارفين
rows.claim: The gnostics connect the believer who combines good and bad deeds to the verse saying God may turn in mercy to such people.
rows.anchor: فهو من الذين خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا وقد قال تعالى فيهم عسى الله أن يتوب عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One should regret one's sins and not presume upon God's mercy, since alongside His vast forgiveness God is severe in force and punishment.
rows.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن يندم على المعاصي الواقعة منه ولا يغتر بالرب الكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows people's circumstances and acts, including lamam, from their creation within Adam from earth and their successive stages as embryos in their mothers' wombs.
rows.anchor: أي خلقكم في ضمن إنشاء أبيكم آدم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajinnah is the plural of janīn, a fetus, literally something buried or concealed in the womb; the word derives from covering, and after birth the child is called a newborn or miscarriage instead.
rows.anchor: والجنين الدفين في الشيء المستتر فيه من جنه إذا ستره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author lists age terms in ordinary Arabic and legal usage: fetus, child, boy, young man, middle-aged man, and elder, with differing age boundaries in language and law.
rows.anchor: هذا في اللغة وفي الشرع يسمى غلاما إلى البلوغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning the mothers' wombs after 'embryos' intensifies the proof of God's knowledge and power: wombs are utterly dark, so knowledge of a fetus there means no state is hidden from Him.
rows.anchor: فإن بطون الأمهات في غاية الظلمة ومن علم حال الجنين فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition follows because freedom from punishment for lamam comes from God's forgiveness despite His knowledge of the sin, not from its being no sin; do not claim total purity or imply immaculate deeds, but thank God for His grace.
rows.anchor: الفاء لترتيب الهي عن تزكية النفس على ما سبق

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says God knows what each soul will do and what it will become; people should neither declare themselves free of sins nor praise their good deeds, which count only when sincerely for God.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن رحمه الله : علم الله من كل نفس ما هي صانعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian couplet reinforces the warning against self-praise: do not claim a pure musk unless you possess it, since quality becomes apparent on its own.
rows.anchor: اكر مسك خالص ندارى مكوى وكرهست خود فاش كردد ببوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic report commands throwing dust in flatterers' faces, meaning people who praise qualities absent from the person praised; dust may be literal or a metaphor for rebuffing them before they become arrogant.
rows.anchor: وأما من زكاه الغير ومدحه فقد ورد فيه (احثوا في وجه المداحين)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations take the command to mean either giving flatterers nothing or paying them to silence them and prevent slander; the author also sees a hint that money is lowly like dust.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد به أن لا يعطوهم شيئا لمدحهم

rows.speaker: أبو الليث
rows.claim: Abū al-Layth distinguishes three kinds of praise: praise to someone's face is forbidden; praise in absence when one knows it will reach them is also forbidden; private praise without concern whether it reaches them is allowed if truthful.
rows.anchor: قال ابو الليث في تفسيره : المدح على ثلاثة أوجه : الأول

rows.speaker: المثنوي
rows.claim: The Mathnawī verses say humans naturally seek praise because the Creator loves thanks and praise; even a person of virtue can be inflated by it, while false praise exposes an empty person.
rows.anchor:
وفي المثنوي :
خلق ما در صورت خود كرد حق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praising someone after death is permissible if it does not exceed bounds, unlike the excessive praise of the Rāfiḍa for the Prophet's family.
rows.anchor: وأما المدح بعد الموت فلا بأس به إذا لم يجاوز الحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows who avoids all sins; the statement reinforces the ban on self-purification and signals that some people in the group fear all sins.
rows.anchor: وهو استئناف مقرر للنهي ومشعر تأن فيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is said that people who boasted of prayer, fasting, and pilgrimage prompted the verse; this applies to self-admiration or ostentation, not gratitude for God's success or joy in obedience.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كان ناس يعملون أعمالا حسنة ثم يقولون

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Najmī gloss contrasts people's finite, faculty-bound general knowledge of themselves with God's unrestricted, detailed knowledge, which is more complete and comprehensive.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية يشير به إلى أن علم الإنسان بنفسه علم إجمالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites the Prophetic report that God created Adam in His image, then notes another version whose wording is left unfinished in this excerpt.
rows.anchor: إن الله خلق آدم على صورته وفي رواية أخرى على صورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed saying cited here says the most beloved people are cheerful and smiling.
rows.anchor: روي أحبكما إلى الطلق البسام

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan warns his son against carefree laughter because his shroud may already have left the fuller's workshop.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن يا ابن آدم تضحك ولعل كفنك خرج

rows.speaker: نوح
rows.claim: Noah wept for three hundred years over his saying that his son belonged to his family.
rows.anchor: وبكي نوح عليه السلام ثلاثمائة سنة بقوله : إن ابني من أهلي

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb says weeping from fear of God until tears run down one's cheeks is dearer than giving away a mountain of gold; what benefits is the heart's weeping, not the eyes alone.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب لأن أبكي من خشية الله حتى تسيل دموعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian couplet urges tears to flow from the eyes and self-cleansing if one has such tears.
rows.anchor: بران ازدوسر شمه ديده جوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God creates death and life; a killer merely breaks bodily structure and connection, while death occurs through God's customary act, and the servant's part is only the acquired act of dismantling the body.
rows.anchor: لا يقدر على الإحياء والإماتة غيره لا خلقا ولا كسبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations say God kills at the appointed time and revives in the grave, creates the causes of death and life, kills unbelievers through denial and revives believers through recognition, or brings about ignorance and knowledge, miserliness and generosity, withholding and giving.
rows.anchor: يا او سازنده اسباب موت وحياتست وكفته اند مرده ميسازد كافر انرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Further reported pairs are fertility and famine, fathers and sons, waking and sleeping, or sperm and the living being.
rows.anchor: وقيل الخصب والجدب أو الآباء والأبناء أو أيقظ وأنام

rows.speaker: المحققون
rows.claim: The realized Sufis interpret death and life as awe and intimacy, or concealment and manifestation.
rows.anchor: ونزد محققان بهيبت وأنس ياباستتار وتجلي

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayrī says God kills ascetics' egos through discipline and revives gnostics' hearts through witnessing, or brings a person to annihilation and gives subsistence through God.
rows.anchor: وأمام قشيري فرموده كه بميراند نفوس زاهد انرا بآثار مجاهدت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inward reading is death of the self from bodily desires and animal pleasures and life of the heart through spiritual qualities and divine character; while the heart fluctuates, self and heart may dominate each other, but in settled assurance the self remains subdued by the heart.
rows.anchor: أو أمات النفس عن الشهوات الجسمانية واللذات الحيوانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death precedes life for rhyme, because sperm precedes the living being, the heart dies before living, and bodily death precedes resurrection in the grave; placing death first also hastens the warning's impact.
rows.anchor: قدم الإماتة على الإحياء رعاية للفاصلة ولأن النطفة قبل النسمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nonexistence precedes existence and existence ends in annihilation; people should not be deceived by a life between two deaths or existence between two absences.
rows.anchor: وأيضا أن العدم قبل الوجود ثم أن مآل الوجود إلى الفناء والعدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase begins the account of God's creation of two human classes, male and female.
rows.anchor: وآنكه خداى تعالى {خلق الزوجين} بيافريد از انسان دو صنف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some commentaries generalize the pair to all animals, but the author objects that not every animal comes from semen, citing birds and the wind from which a hen's egg is formed.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض التفاسير من كل الحيوان وفيه أن كل حيوان لا يخلق من النطفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pair means male and female; nutfa is clear water, commonly used for a man's semen, and tamnā means flowing or spilling into the womb.
rows.anchor: هي الماء الصافي ويعبر بها عن ماء الرجل كما في المفردات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb derives from amnā, to emit semen; Adam, Eve, and Jesus are exceptions to birth from a semen drop. Tamannā may also mean that God determines which drop will become a child.
rows.anchor: وآدم وحوا وعيسى عليهما السلام ازين مستثنى اند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Sufi allusion makes male the active spirit and female the receptive soul; their conjunction yields a sound heart capable of worldly and otherworldly aims, as a seed settles in the womb of eternal will.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أنه تعالى خلق زوج ذكر الروح موصوفا بصفة الفاعلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, 'when it is measured or emitted' describes the seed moving in the womb of primordial will or being determined by eternal wisdom.
rows.anchor: إذا تمنى إذا تحرك وتدفق في رحم الإرادة القديمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Male is mentioned first for rhyme and rank, although the world is fundamentally feminine and that quality pervades it; elders loved women because femininity is more manifest in them.
rows.anchor: قدم الذكر رعاية للفاصلة ولشرفه الرتبى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses served ten years as a woman's dowry, and even a great king adopts a posture of prostration in intercourse; since all worlds have literal or figurative union, half of creation is male and half female, or agent and receptacle, with humanity as their isthmus.
rows.anchor: حتى آجر موسى عليه السلام نفسه في مهر امرأة عشر سنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other creation is resurrection after death, which God fulfills by promise; the word 'upon' does not imply an obligation imposed on God.
rows.anchor: وهو لإحياء بعد الموت وفاء بوعده لا لأنه يجب على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine wisdom requires a second bodily creation for recompense and for believers to reach fitting perfection gradually; the world could not contain even one person's full reward, so demanding immediate results is discourteous, though a purified divine gift should be accepted and good lies in God's choice.
rows.anchor: وفيه تصريح بأن الحكمة الإلهية اقتضت النشأة الثانية الصورية للجزاء والمكافأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Just as bodily resurrection follows complete bodily annihilation and readiness for spirit, spiritual resurrection—subsistence and divine attributes—requires full spiritual annihilation, shedding human traits, and readiness for divine effusion.
rows.anchor: فكذا النشأة الأخرى المعنوية وهي البقاء والاتصاف بالصفات الإلهية موقوفة على تمام الفناء المعنوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both resurrections require a sound constitution: a malformed embryo miscarries and a malformed womb cannot conceive; Jesus says none enters heaven's kingdom without being born twice, meaning entry into heavenly realities, lights, and secrets through the second birth of prophets and saints.
rows.anchor: وإلى الولادة الثانية التي هي النشأة الأخرى أشار عيسى عليه السلام بقوله
